messages:
hana: Heads-up — ACME reported their monthly credits hit 0 unexpectedly during a long streaming job, then refilled 2 hours later instead of at midnight local TZ. Customer is seeing repeated 429s. Attaching quick logs below.
trent (eng): Can you paste the tenant id and example request pattern? streaming/ws or REST?
hana: Tenant: acme-inc (tenant_789). They use a long websocket stream with reconnection retries. Sample server log: 
```
[2026-03-01T22:58:12Z] tenant=tenant_789 tokens_used=+4500 request=streaming.websocket chunk=...
[2026-03-01T23:01:09Z] tenant=tenant_789 response=429 code=QUOTA_EXHAUSTED remaining=0
[2026-03-01T23:01:12Z] tenant=tenant_789 reconnect attempt=1 tokens_used=+150
[2026-03-01T23:03:45Z] tenant=tenant_789 response=429 remaining=0
```
hana: Customer says their billing timezone is America/Los_Angeles and they expected reset at 00:00 PST but it refilled at 02:00.
maria (billing): Did they change plan or get a prorate/top-up around the boundary? That can shift visible refill times.
hana: They did a promo top-up on 2026-03-01 23:50 PST (internal note: promo_23). But UI showed 0 and API 429 for ~2 hours after midnight.
trent (eng): Likely interplay between edge cache + background refill job + long-lived websocket token accounting. If stream reconnects increment tokens after midnight, the refill job could run but cache could still report zero until edge TTL expires. Can you capture API responses header `x-quota-refill-ts` and any edge cache hits?
hana: I have curl example showing headers: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 08:01:09 GMT
x-quota-window-start: 2026-03-01T08:00:00Z
x-quota-remaining: 0
x-edge-cache: HIT
```

hana: After we forced a cache flush for tenant_789, API started returning remaining=1200 and customer reconnected fine.
ryan (sre): Noted. What was the cache TTL and which edge node? Need to know for mitigation. Also want repro steps for the dev env.
hana: Edge node: edge-us-west-2a, ttl=120s. Repro steps I used: 1) simulate long stream using websocket generating ~5k tokens; 2) force reconnect loop with 2s backoff for 10 attempts; 3) trigger promo top-up API at 23:50 PST; 4) observe 429s after midnight until cache invalidation.
trent (eng): Thanks. Hypothesis: refill job executes -> increments backend counter, but edge cache still serves zero to API router until TTL or explicit invalidation. Combined with reconnects that continue to consume tokens, customer sees short window of continued 429s. Two mitigations: 1) invalidate tenant cache on refill/top-up (cheap hook), 2) ensure refill timestamp is returned in response header so clients can choose to retry after the exact time.
maria (billing): We can add a webhook on promo/top-up to call cache invalidation. I'll scope with product.
hana: For now, suggested temporary workaround to customer: wait 60-120s then reconnect OR call our support endpoint to force cache refresh: `POST /internal/tenants/tenant_789/refresh-cache` (requires auth). They did that and recovered.
trent (eng): Filed issue INF-2418 to add cache invalidation on refill and add `x-quota-refill-ts` header to the API. Also adding a note in support KB about long-lived streams + retry storms around reset boundaries.
hana: Created a short KB note and pinged the customer with repro and workaround. They want ETA on full fix.
maria (billing): We'll aim for hotfix next sprint; I'll update ETA once engineering owners confirm.
hana: Thanks all — marking as high priority. Assigning follow-ups: INF-2418 (trent), billing webhook (maria), SRE validation (ryan). support-bot: Reminder set: follow up in 7 days.
